name: Centro Historico
tagline: The pink-stone heart where it all happens
description: The UNESCO-listed core, a maze of cobbled callejones climbing between the baroque cathedral, plazas, museums, and cantinas. This is where nomads will want to base themselves, with the best cafes, walkability, and nightlife, all wrapped in genuinely spectacular colonial architecture and evening callejoneadas.
bestFor: First-time visitors and short-to-medium stays who want everything on foot

name: Alameda
tagline: Leafy, local, and a short walk from the center
description: Centered on the Alameda Garcia de la Cadena park just southwest of the core, this area mixes green space, everyday shops, and residential streets. It offers a slightly calmer, more local feel than the tourist center while staying within easy walking or a quick bus of the cathedral and plazas.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local life near the center

name: Cerro de la Bufa
description: The dramatic hill crowning the city, reached by road, footpaths, or the teleferico cable car. Home to sweeping viewpoints, a chapel, and the site of the famous 1914 battle. It is more a destination than a residential base, but the neighborhoods on its slopes offer unbeatable panoramas over the ravine.
bestFor: Those prioritizing views and quiet over central convenience
cons: Steep and far from daily services

name: Guadalupe
tagline: Adjacent town with the grand convent
description: A separate municipality just east of Zacatecas, effectively part of the metro area and linked by frequent buses. Home to the magnificent Convento de Guadalupe and its art museum, it offers a quieter, more spread-out, and affordable base with everyday amenities, trading central charm for space and lower costs.
bestFor: Budget-focused longer stays who do not mind commuting to Centro
